Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the product walkthrough. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) SOC 2: We require SOC 2 Type II for any vendor with access to PHI. Yes, we generally ask for the latest 12-month period report.
2) HIPAA: We do have HIPAA-covered workloads; we'll need a BAA in place for any environment processing PHI.
3) Deletion SLAs: Our procurement/security target is:
   - Primary user data: deletion confirmation within 30 days of request.
   - Application logs/diagnostics: retention capped at 90 days by default.
   - Backups: we need confirmation on how backups are handled and an expected window for purge — ideally backups should be purged within 30 days after the retention window, but we understand some backup systems have constraints.
4) Vendor questionnaire: attaching our standard security questionnaire (PDF). Please have your security/compliance team complete and return.

Also include any standard SLA language/commitments you can provide about data purges from backups and immutable snapshots. Procurement will review the questionnaire once completed.

Best,

Hi all — thanks for the clear asks. Answers below and attached artifacts.

1) SOC 2:
- Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering the period ending 2025-12-31. I’ve attached the report stub here for your review. [Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_Report_2025.pdf]

2) HIPAA / BAA:
- We support HIPAA-covered workloads and can sign a BAA. The BAA covers processing and controls for PHI; we typically include the environment/regions and roles that will process PHI.

3) Data deletion SLAs and retention (proposed):
- Primary user data (customer-managed datasets / user-generated content): deletion confirmed within 30 days of request, including removal from active storage and primary databases.
- Application logs / diagnostics: default retention 90 days. If you require shorter retention we can configure per-contract.
- Backups / snapshots: standard backup retention is 180 days by default. We can commit to purging customer data from backups within 30 days after the requested retention window where technically feasible. Note: immutable snapshot stores and cold backups may have compliance constraints that require coordination; in those cases we provide an auditable schedule and a guaranteed purge window documented in the SLA.

4) Limitations and recommended contract language:
- For guaranteed deletion from all backups including offsite cold storage, include a 30–45 day purge window in the contract to allow for safe restore/testing processes and to avoid data corruption.
- We recommend the following clause for the SLA: 
  "Redwood will remove customer-identifiable data from active storage within 30 days of deletion request and will take commercially reasonable steps to purge such data from backups and immutable snapshots within 45 days where technical constraints exist. Redwood will provide certification of purge upon request."

5) Vendor questionnaire:
- I've completed our responses and attached the filled questionnaire. [Attachment: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Filled.pdf]
- Also attaching a compact SLA table that maps each retention type to proposed windows for your contracting team. [Attachment: Data_Retention_SLA_Table.xlsx]

Next steps:
- If this looks good, Marissa — suggest we schedule a 30-minute session with Samantha + procurement to walk the SLA table and next steps on BAA/contracting.

Happy to answer any follow-ups.

Thanks,
